qs.q:
Interview — Ted Finch

"I was top of the class in English, and I was interested enough in art to sit fairly still during the lesson; otherwise, I couldn't wait for when we went to the gym."

Finch's favourite subject at school was…
A physical exercise.
B science.
C English.
D art.

Ted Finch

"I could have walked away from it all, it's true, but I had no sense of direction and couldn't think of an alternative. So I enrolled to study English."

Finch went to university because…
A he wanted to study English.
B he wanted to be like his father.
C it was expected of him.
D he didn't know what else to do.
opts: he wanted to be like his father.
he didn't know what else to do.

qs.q:
Ted Finch

"It was a difficult time for me. I didn't feel that I was going anywhere, or doing anything with my life. I needed a new direction."

Finch dropped out of university because…
A the course was hard for him.
B he thought he was wasting his time.
C he wanted to travel.
D he found himself a job.
opts: the course was hard for him.
he thought he was wasting his time.

qs.q:
Ted Finch

"You meet so many different types of people and see into their lives, which gave me lots of material for my future books."

Finch thinks his job as a journalist…
A gave him useful experience.
B gave him a sense of direction.
C made him popular locally.
D improved his writing style.
opts: gave him a sense of direction.

qs.q:
Ted Finch

"I wanted to use fantasy so we see the REALITIES OF OUR SOCIETY from a different perspective."

Finch thinks that his fantasy books…
A are an escape from the realities of life.
B are not real literature.
C reflect the world we live in.
D are just for entertainment.
opts: are an escape from the realities of life.
reflect the world we live in.

qs.q:
Ted Finch

"I can't imagine myself not writing my annual book. It's something I just have to do. Don't ask me why."

Finch writes one book a year…
A for financial reasons.
B so as not to get bored.
C because it gives him something to do.
D because he can't help himself.
opts: so as not to get bored.
because it gives him something to do.

qs.q:
Energy Efficiency

"'Energy efficiency' is often used to describe any energy-saving measure. However, it should be distinguished from energy conservation. (19) ___ Examples include turning down a thermostat in the winter or walking to the shops."

A Non-domestic buildings need a focus on ventilation and air-conditioning.
B In many cases this initial investment will be paid back in the form of reduced energy costs.
C The savings may vary considerably.
D Switching from a 90% efficient gas boiler to a 100% efficient electric heater may increase energy use.
E The potential exists for further improvements.
F Whether it results in energy savings depends on what you do with the money you saved.
G For instance, a hot pipe containing a chemical that needs to be cooled can be used to warm up other chemicals.
H That's a broader term which not only includes changing efficiency but also dropping a service.
opts: A — Non-domestic buildings need a focus on ventilation.
B — In many cases initial investment paid back in reduced energy costs.
C — The savings may vary considerably.
D — Switching from gas boiler to electric heater may increase energy use.
E — The potential exists for further improvements.
F — Whether it results in savings depends on what you do with money saved.
G — A hot pipe can be used to warm up other chemicals.
H — That's a broader term — changing efficiency but also dropping a service.
